newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Nearly 40 hurt as bomb blasts rock Bangladesh port.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 40 hurt as bomb blasts rock Bangladesh port.

text.p: Nearly 40 people were injured in bomb blasts and clashes between rival activists during an opposition-led general strike on Tuesday in the port city of Chittagong and neighbouring areas, police said.
They said activists of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) exchanged gunfire and fought sporadic battles with supporters of the ruling Awami League.
The BNP supporters ransacked railway offices, damaged a locomotive and attacked an Awami League office in Chittagong, witnesses said.
"Up to 40 people have been injured and police arrested at least 15 activists," one officer in Chittagong said.
Violence was also reported from outlying districts but no details were available, police told reporters.
Frequent bomb blasts shook the city and a number of vehicles carrying workers to the Chittagong Export Processing Zone (EPZ) were attacked and damaged, witnesss said.
Operations in the EPZ, which has 70 foreign industrial units, were badly affected as 80 percent of workers could not report for duty, officials said.
Work at the port was partially affected, said Captain Zahiruddin Mahmud, chairman of the Chittagong Port Authority.
A police vehicle was bombed on Monday night by unidentified attackers near the port, wounding two people, police said.
Witnesses and officials said business came to a virtual standstill on Tuesday across southeast Bangladesh because of the daylong strike.
Trains, ferries and buses were halted, transport operators said. Air flights from Dhaka, however, operated on schedule, they told reporters.
Chittagong Stock Exchange, commercial centres, industries, educational institutions, banks, and most of the government and private offices were closed.

BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia called for the dawn-to-dusk stoppage to protest against what she said was "government-led terrorism and the ruling (Awami League) party's subservient policies towards India."
Khaleda has accused Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of being pro-Indian, jeopardising Bangladesh's national security.
"This is a near-total strike," said one Chittagong journalist who went round the city.
Khaleda said she called the strike only in the greater Chittagong division because that was the area most affected by "government-led terrorism". She did not elaborate.
The BNP says the government has been persecuting political opponents, jailing thousands.
One senior BNP official said last week ruling party thugs had killed nearly 200 party workers and supporters since it came to power last June, a charge the government denies.
Khaleda said on Saturday that May 6 would "serve as a warning to this autocratic government and will be followed up, if necessary".
The strike did not affect other parts of the country.
